Genetic and research-related clinical information is highly sensitive, and if the EMR stores more detailed genetics-related context than is functionally necessary for ongoing care, this constitutes excessive sensitive data disclosure/processing.
assumptions: Assumes some of the context-relevant research details may exceed the minimum necessary content needed in the EMR.
uncertainty_note: The description does not specify the exact scope or minimum necessary dataset, so excess sensitivity is plausible but not certain.

title: Patients may be unaware of the granularity or purpose of genetics-related recommendations stored in the EMR
description: The flow records context-relevant research data and genetic physician recommendations in the Internal EMR. If patients are not clearly informed that such detailed genetics-related recommendations and next-step information are stored for care and potentially related purposes, they may lack awareness of the granularity and purpose of processing.
assumptions: Assumes notice to patients about this specific EMR recording practice may be incomplete or not sufficiently specific.
uncertainty_note: No transparency or notice information is provided, so this is a conditional risk rather than a confirmed deficiency.

title: Recording genetics-related research context in the EMR may violate minimization or purpose-limitation principles
description: If the Internal EMR stores context-relevant research data together with clinical recommendations beyond what is necessary for patient care, the processing may conflict with data-protection principles such as data minimization and purpose limitation, creating compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes some research-context details may not be necessary for the EMR's clinical purpose.
uncertainty_note: This compliance risk depends on whether the stored research context is necessary and covered by an appropriate lawful basis or governance framework, which is not specified.

title: Physical sample may be retained longer than necessary after retrieval trigger
description: The flow moves the remainder of a physical sample into Physical Sample Storage after contextual retention requirements have been met. If the sample is stored beyond what is strictly necessary for the stated purpose, the storage and continued processing of personal material may exceed needed retention duration.
assumptions: Assumes the physical sample can constitute personal data or personal material linked to a data subject, and that storage continues after the retention checkpoint rather than immediate destruction or irreversible anonymization.
uncertainty_note: The wording 'retrieve the remainder of the physical sample once contextual retention requirements have been met' is ambiguous; this threat applies if the flow results in continued storage/retention rather than compliant disposal.

title: Data subjects may lack effective control over continued storage or disposal of remainder samples
description: If remainder physical samples are placed into storage after retention-related conditions are reached, data subjects may have limited ability to understand, request, or verify whether the sample is retained, returned, or destroyed, undermining intervenability over continued handling of their material.
assumptions: Assumes the sample is tied to an identifiable person and that policy or user-facing controls about post-retention handling are limited or absent.
uncertainty_note: No explicit transparency or control context is provided; this is a plausible risk only if individuals are not given meaningful post-collection retention/disposal controls.

title: Potential storage-limitation or data-minimization violation for retained remainder samples
description: Storing the remainder of a physical sample after contextual retention requirements have been met may conflict with data-protection principles if the sample is kept longer, in greater amount, or for broader purposes than necessary.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy regulation covers the physical sample and that the flow represents ongoing retention instead of destruction according to policy.
uncertainty_note: This compliance threat depends on regulatory treatment of the sample and on whether the post-threshold action is retention rather than mandated archival or disposal.

title: Disposed sample record may be retained longer than necessary
description: Even though the flow's purpose is disposal of the remaining physical sample after retention requirements are met, storing the disposal item in the destination data store may still result in personal or sample-linked information being kept beyond what is functionally necessary if the store retains detailed disposal records indefinitely.
uncertainty_note: Applies if the Sample Disposal Item data store keeps personal or sample-linked disposal records rather than merely effectuating destruction; the flow description does not specify retention controls on the store.

title: Data subjects may lack effective control over final deletion of sample-linked data
description: If disposal of the physical sample is represented by a stored disposal item, data subjects may be unable to verify, influence, or obtain actual deletion of remaining sample-linked information, especially if records about the sample persist after physical destruction.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether data subjects are expected to have deletion/intervention rights over sample-disposal records; the prompt does not state any user-facing controls.

title: Storage-limitation and data-minimization risk in disposal record keeping
description: If the destination data store preserves identifiable or linkable details about disposed physical samples after contextual retention requirements have already been satisfied, the system may violate storage-limitation or data-minimization principles by continuing to process more data, or for longer, than necessary for the disposal function.
uncertainty_note: This compliance risk is inferred from the disposal/retention context; the actual lawful basis, retention schedule, and necessity of keeping disposal records are not provided.

title: Residual physical sample retained on reused flow cell
description: If used flow cells are not fully cleaned after sequencing, residual biological material may remain on the stored/reused flow cell longer than functionally necessary. That residual material can disclose personal or genetic information during later handling or reuse, contrary to the stated need to eliminate remnants after the run.
assumptions: A used flow cell may contain residual physical sample material that can still reveal personal/genetic data if retained.

title: Residual sample on flow cell accessible during subsequent reuse or handling
description: A used flow cell containing leftover sample material may make personal/genetic data accessible to people or processes handling the datastore item later, including in a subsequent sequencing run. This is broader accessibility than necessary for the cleaning/storage function and creates a disclosure risk.
assumptions: Subsequent technicians or processes may access or reuse the same physical flow cell.

title: Covert downstream processing/disclosure via residual sample remnants
description: If residual sample remains on a reused flow cell, the data subject would typically have no transparency that physical remnants of their sample could be processed or disclosed in later runs or handling. This creates unawareness about secondary processing/disclosure of their material.
assumptions: The original data subject is not specifically informed that residual material could persist on reused consumables.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether the organization provides explicit notice about residual-risk handling of physical consumables; that is not stated.

title: Potential violation of storage-limitation and data-minimization principles
description: Failure to remove residual physical sample material from used flow cells would keep personal/genetic material beyond what is needed for the completed sequencing run and could expose it during reuse. That suggests a potential compliance issue with data minimization and storage-limitation principles.
assumptions: Residual biological material is treated as personal data or a source of personal data under the applicable regime.
uncertainty_note: Regulatory qualification of residual biological material depends on jurisdiction and whether it is considered personal data in context.

title: Derived context-relevant research data may remain linkable to an individual
description: The compute nodes transform raw sequence data into context-relevant research data. Even if direct identifiers are not mentioned, analysis of sequence-derived data can create profiles or distinctive feature sets that allow records concerning the same individual to be linked across processing runs or datasets.
assumptions: Sequence data and derived research data concern individuals and may preserve sufficiently distinctive attributes for linkage.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not explicitly state whether identifiers are removed or whether data is human genomic/personal sequence data; applicability depends on the distinctiveness of the derived data.

title: Stored research data may indirectly identify a data subject through content or metadata
description: When context-relevant research data is written to the cluster filesystem, the stored content or associated metadata may reveal identity indirectly, for example through sample identifiers, project metadata, provenance, or highly distinctive sequence-derived characteristics.
assumptions: The cluster filesystem stores file names, metadata, or payload content that may contain sample- or subject-associated information.
uncertainty_note: No explicit identifiers are described in the flow; this threat is based on likely indirect identifiers or metadata in research datasets.

title: Filesystem persistence and attributable metadata may create non-repudiable evidence of data generation
description: Writing the output to the cluster filesystem may retain timestamps, ownership, path, provenance, or audit information linking the generated research data to a particular processing action, operator, or subject-related record, reducing deniability.
assumptions: The filesystem or surrounding infrastructure keeps persistent file metadata or audit logs attributable to actors or records.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not explicitly mention audit logging; this depends on normal filesystem or cluster auditing behavior.

title: Transfer of sequence-derived data to storage may be network-observable
description: The movement of data from compute nodes to the cluster filesystem may be observable as network traffic or storage I/O patterns, allowing an observer to detect that sensitive sequence processing or a specific dataset write is occurring even without seeing the payload.
assumptions: The compute nodes and cluster filesystem communicate over an observable network or fabric, and traffic patterns are accessible to an attacker or untrusted operator.
uncertainty_note: If the storage path is fully internal and strongly protected against observation, this threat may be reduced.

title: Transformation into context-relevant research data may disclose more than is necessary
description: The processing step explicitly creates context-relevant research data from raw sequence data. Such enrichment or transformation can expose additional inferred or contextual personal information beyond what is strictly necessary for storage or the immediate computational task.
assumptions: The derived research data contains added contextual, analytical, or inferred information about individuals rather than merely a minimal intermediate representation.
uncertainty_note: The description indicates contextualization, but it does not specify whether all derived fields are necessary.

title: Stored research data may be accessible more broadly than necessary on the cluster filesystem
description: Persisting sequence-derived research data in a cluster filesystem can increase exposure if stored files are readable by more users, jobs, administrators, or services than functionally required, leading to disclosure of sensitive research data.
assumptions: The cluster filesystem is shared infrastructure with potentially broad read/access paths.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not specify access controls; risk depends on actual filesystem permissions and isolation.

title: Granularity and purpose of deriving context-relevant research data may not be transparent to data subjects

If data subjects were not informed about this derivation, contextual enrichment, or the level of detail produced, they may be unaware of the true scope and purpose of processing.

uncertainty_note: No notice or consent information is provided, so this is a plausible transparency risk rather than a confirmed issue.

assumptions: The processed sequence data is personal data and the derived research data may exceed the necessary scope for the legitimate purpose.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on the lawful basis, stated research purpose, and whether safeguards and minimization are actually in place.

uncertainty_note: Whether this disclosure is necessary cannot be determined from the flow alone, but exposure to an external party is explicit.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that their final clinical report is disclosed to a third-party portal

title: Sharing the final clinical report with a third-party portal may lack an established lawful basis or required safeguards
